issues.failure_explanation: Gershgorin's theorem bounds only the eigenvalues of a $\mu$-diagonally dominant matrix, hence the spectral radius of $A^{-1}$ ($\le 1/\mu$); it does not bound an operator norm of $A^{-1}$. For non-normal matrices the smallest singular value can be strictly smaller than the smallest eigenvalue modulus, and one can construct $\mu$-row-diagonally dominant matrices (even M-matrices with the sign pattern of $D\cR$) with $\|A^{-1}\|_2 > 1/\mu$. The norm in the statement is unspecified, and the proof never establishes any operator-norm estimate. The bound that is actually used downstream (in the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:exist-uniqueness-scheme-gen}) is the $\ell^\infty$ operator-norm bound $\|A^{-1}\|_\infty \le 1/\mu$, which is true for row-$\mu$-diagonally dominant matrices but only via the direct estimate $\|Ax\|_\infty \ge \mu\|x\|_\infty$ (take a row $i$ with $|x_i| = \|x\|_\infty$), a step the proof omits.

failure_location.quote: By Gershgorin theorem, if $A$ is $\mu$-diagonally dominant, all the eigenvalues of $A$ have complex modulus bigger or equal than $\mu$, and therefore, $A$ is invertible with $\| A^{-1}\| \leq \frac{1}{\mu}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the estimate for the $\ell^\infty$ operator norm and replace the Gershgorin-based norm inference with the standard row-dominance estimate $\|D\cR(u)x\|_\infty \ge \mu\|x\|_\infty$ (Varah-type, three lines), keeping Gershgorin only for invertibility.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative inverse bound of Lemma \ref{lem:DR-invertible} is unproved as written and is false if the unspecified norm is read as, e.g., the 2-norm. No downstream result is invalidated: the Hadamard/Pourciau arguments in Theorem \ref{thm:exist-uniqueness-scheme-gen} explicitly use the $\infty$-norm bound, which is valid by the standard argument.
issues.title: Gershgorin eigenvalue bound does not yield the claimed operator-norm bound on (D R)^{-1}
issues.why_classification: A short, local, standard repair (specify the norm; insert the classical $\infty$-norm dominance estimate) leaves the lemma's statement, its proof architecture, and every dependent claim unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation:
With the stated transform $v = (1 - e^{-\lambda u})/\lambda$ one has $v_t = e^{-\lambda u} u_t$ and $
abla v = e^{-\lambda u}
abla u$, hence $v_t + \|
abla v\| = e^{-\lambda u}(u_t + \|
abla u\|) = 0$. Therefore $v_t + \lambda v + \|
abla v\| = \lambda v = 1 - e^{-\lambda u}$, which vanishes only where $u = 0$; for any nonzero solution (e.g. $u(x,t) = |x| - t$ on $t < |x|$) the claimed transformed equation fails, so the displayed equivalence is false. Unlike the stationary case, where the source $f(x) > 0$ generates the zero-order term $\lambda f v$, the homogeneous evolution equation generates no $\lambda v$ term (the pointwise-in-time transform of $u_t$ cannot produce one).

Replace the display by the equation the stated transform actually gives, $v_t + \|

issues.overall_effect: A standalone displayed claim in the strong-monotonicity remarks is false, and the suggestion that this transform yields a strongly monotone time-dependent eikonal equation is incorrect as stated. No theorem, proof, algorithm, or numerical experiment uses this display: Section 3 treats time-dependent problems via (F1)-(F3), which needs no zero-order term when $\cF$ is independent of $u$.
issues.title: Kruzhkov transform of u_t + ||grad u|| = 0 produces no lambda v term
issues.why_classification: The false claim is an isolated display in a remark section; the correction is local, and no formal result or downstream argument depends on it, so all substantive claims survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By using similar arguments as for the stability of the steady state case.

issues.failure_explanation: Under (F1)-(F3), $\cF$ may decrease in $u$ with $\dt\,\cF_u$ as low as $-\lambda$, $\lambda \in (0,1)$. The steady-state comparison argument invoked as the proof relies on (H3)'s positive lower bound $\ml(u-v)$; here the zero-order lower bound is negative, so at an interior maximum $M$ of $u^{n+1}-v^{n+1}$ the correct comparison gives only $(1-\lambda)M \le \|u^n - v^n\|_\infty + \dt\|\cR(u)^{n+1}\|_\infty$, i.e. an amplification factor $(1-\lambda)^{-1}$ per step that the statement omits. The stated estimate is false as written: take a single interior node, no spatial coupling, $\cF(x,u,p) = -(\lambda/\dt)u$ (satisfies (F1)-(F3)), equal boundary data and $u^n = v^n$; then $(1-\lambda)(u^{n+1}-v^{n+1}) = \dt\,\cR(u)^{n+1}$, so the actual difference $\dt\|\cR\|/(1-\lambda)$ exceeds the claimed bound $\dt\|\cR\|$. The displayed recursion derived from the estimate inherits the same error.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the one-step bound with the amplification factor, e.g. $\|u^{n+1}-v^{n+1}\|_\infty \le \max\big(\|\bar b^{n+1}-\bar c^{n+1}\|_{\ell^\infty(\cB)}, (1-\lambda)^{-1}(\|u^n-v^n\|_\infty + \dt\|\cR(u)^{n+1}\|_\infty)\big)$, prove it by the same interior-maximum comparison using (F2)-(F3), and derive the recursion via a discrete Gronwall argument, giving stability constants $(1-\lambda)^{-n}$ ($\approx e^{CT}$ when (F3) holds with $\lambda = C\dt$); note the constant-1 bound remains valid when $\cF_u \ge 0$.
issues.overall_effect: The one-step stability estimate, the unlabelled recursion $\|u^n-v^n\|_\infty \le \|u^0-v^0\|_\infty + \sum_m \max(\dt\|\cR(u)^m\|_\infty, \|\bar b^m-\bar c^m\|_{\cB})$, and the resulting a posteriori error bound for implicit time-stepping are unreliable whenever $\cF$ is not non-decreasing in $u$; the claimed constant-1 stability is lost. The estimate holds only in the special case $\cF_u \ge 0$. No labelled result depends on it: Theorem \ref{thm:added-1} and Corollary \ref{cor:added-1} (existence/uniqueness) are unaffected.
issues.title: Time-dependent stability estimate is false under (F1)-(F3): missing (1-lambda)^{-1} amplification
issues.why_classification: The statement is false as written, but a contained standard argument (comparison plus discrete Gronwall) yields a recognizably comparable stability and a posteriori error estimate with a $T$-dependent constant in place of 1; no new global proof architecture is needed and no other labelled result is affected.
